name: Standardized Git workflows can mirror client repositories and synchronize commits under intended personas

attribution.legal_posture: Defensive synthesis of cited public sources; the technique mapping supplies context rather than an identity attribution.

caveats: Commit metadata can be rewritten during legitimate rebases, migrations, pair programming, or by bots; authorship anomalies require corroboration before account-sharing attribution.
False-positive caution: Repository mirroring, backups, migrations, monorepo tooling, and CI systems are legitimate. Baseline by role and approved destination.

statements: GitLab reports standardized tooling used to mirror private repositories and synchronize commits under intended developer identities, both reducing persona mistakes and retaining copies of client code. This combines code theft risk, shared-team operation, and authorship manipulation more specifically than generic repository reuse.
